parafin: Embedded small-business financing, founded by former Robinhood engineers (San Francisco). Parafin's own Series B post names 'Series A and seed lead investors, Thrive Capital and Ribbit Capital', so Ribbit led the seed and Thrive the Series A, announced together in September 2021 as a $34M Series Seed and A financing (https://www.parafin.com/blog/parafin-series-a-financing). Graduated: the Series A, then the $60M Series B led by GIC in August 2022 (the company's post). Ribbit joined the $100M Series C of December 2024 led by Notable Capital (FinTech Global), at a $750M valuation (Bloomberg, 2024-12-17), so below_1b. Redpoint's book carries $1.5B for a '$125M Series C' from a Parafin page that no longer loads; the web check of 2026-09-28 found no report of that figure or of any later round, so this row stands and Redpoint's is the side to align. Momentum check: no round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28.
gusto: Payroll, benefits and HR software (San Francisco; ZenPayroll until 2015). Ribbit came in as a new investor in ZenPayroll's $60M round of April 2015 led by Google Capital, beside new investor Emergence and existing investors General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins and Google Ventures (CPA Practice Advisor 2015-04-06); that round followed the seed and the $20M Series A of 2014 (General Catalyst's book), so the entry is Growth (medium, the article gives no series letter). Two pre-filled values are wrong joins: the country NL (Wikidata matched a Dutch entity) and the 10b_plus band at $10B (an aggregator figure). The freshest priced event is the June 2025 employee tender offer at $9.3B, $200M led by Teachers' Venture Growth (Fortune, 2025-06-09), so 1b_plus; the last primary was the Series E at $9.5B in August 2021. The a16z and Felicis books still carry 10b_plus at $10B, the stale side for rule 10.

vouch: Vouch Insurance, business insurance for startups founded by Sam Hodges, San Francisco. Operating and private: it raised $25M in a round led by Ribbit in March 2024 (FinTech Global), and in August 2025 agreed to sell its MGA (Corix) and its carrier subsidiary to Hiscox USA, subject to regulatory approval, while Vouch continues as an independent broker (Coverager). No valuation at or above $1B found. First Round's 'Vouch' (a 2015 social-lending startup) is another company; Y Combinator's 'Vouch' is this company (Summer 2019 batch, vouch.us, legal name SV Instech, Inc., 'Active' in the YC directory); its defunct status was carried from First Round's namesake, so Y Combinator's row is the side to align.
